# Draft:Nepali Heritage Day (British Columbia) Canada

Nepali Heritage Day (British Columbia)
Nepali Heritage Day is an officially recognized observance in the Canadian province of British Columbia, proclaimed to be held on May 29 beginning in 2026. The day recognizes the cultural, social, and economic contributions of people of Nepali heritage to British Columbia.
The proclamation was issued by the Government of British Columbia under the authority of the Crown and forms part of the province’s multicultural recognition initiatives.
Background
May 29 holds significance for the global Nepali community as it commemorates the first successful ascent of Mount Everest in 1953 by Tenzing Norgay Sherpa, a Nepali citizen, and Sir Edmund Hillary. The date is widely observed by Nepali communities worldwide as a symbol of Nepali heritage, resilience, and cultural identity.
Proclamation
In January 2026, the Government of British Columbia officially proclaimed May 29, 2026, as Nepali Heritage Day in the province. The proclamation acknowledges the role of Nepali Canadians in British Columbia’s social, cultural, political, and economic life.
The proclamation also reflects British Columbia’s commitment to multiculturalism and inclusion by formally recognizing the heritage of one of the province’s growing cultural communities.
Observance
The first official observance of Nepali Heritage Day in British Columbia is scheduled to take place on May 29, 2026, at the Legislative Assembly of British Columbia, Hall of Honour. Community organizations and representatives are expected to participate in cultural and educational activities marking the day.
